title: Detection of Genetic Variation Using PNA Probe-Based Melting Point Analysis
author: Hur, Kim, et al.
materials: Hybridization between probes and synthetic oligonucleotide targets was performed in a CFX96™ Real-Time System (BIO-RAD, USA). To analyze the Tm of PNA probe, synthetic single-stranded DNA oligomers were directly used as the target DNA. A thermal cyclic reaction was performed using the following conditions: the 20 μL reactions contained 1X SSB Real-Time FMCA™ buffer (SeaSun Biomaterials, Korea), 0.5 μM PNA probe, and 0.5 μL of DNA template (1 × 105 copies of synthetic DNA). Melting point analysis began with a denaturation step of 3 min at 95 °C; a stepwise hybridization and followed by a stepwise temperature increase up to 85 °C at 0.5 °C/step with a 5 s interval between each step (Additional file 4: Figure S1). The target oligomers and probes used are listed in Additional file 2: Table S1.

steps.title: Prepare serial DNA dilutions
steps.instruction: Dilute synthetic single‑stranded DNA to obtain templates ranging from 1 × 10⁸ to 1 × 10² copies per reaction and also prepare a 1 × 10⁵‑copy template for direct Tm measurement.

substeps.instruction: Take the stock synthetic DNA and perform 10‑fold serial dilutions to achieve concentrations of 1 × 10⁸, 1 × 10⁷, 1 × 10⁶, 1 × 10⁵, 1 × 10⁴, 1 × 10³, and 1 × 10² copies per 0.5 µL aliquot.
Aliquot 0.5 µL of the 1 × 10⁵‑copy dilution for the direct melting‑point (Tm) analysis.

steps.title: Set up FMCA reaction mixture
steps.instruction: In a CFX96™ Real‑Time System (Bio‑Rad, USA), assemble 20 µL reactions containing 1X SSB Real‑Time FMCA™ buffer (SeaSun Biomaterials, Korea), 0.5 µM PNA probe, and 0.5 µL of the appropriate DNA template; run each condition in four replicates.

steps.title: Run thermal cycling and melting analysis
steps.instruction: Program the instrument for a 3‑minute denaturation at 95 °C, followed by stepwise hybridization with a temperature increase to 85 °C at 0.5 °C per step, holding 5 seconds at each step.

substeps.instruction: Increase temperature from the annealing point to 85 °C in 0.5 °C increments, pausing 5 s at each increment.

steps.title: Collect fluorescence data for quantification
steps.instruction: Measure fluorescence intensity during the melting step (instead of the amplification step) and record the primer‑annealing fluorescence point for each replicate to generate amplification and melting curves for quantitative analysis.

substeps.instruction: Capture fluorescence at the primer‑annealing step of each PCR cycle.
Use the melting‑step fluorescence values to construct melting curves and calculate Tm values.
Compile data from the four replicates to produce quantitative amplification and standard curves.
